kata.name: Iterator parity ceiling - the same replay fault with a complete conventional sample; the probe buys nothing
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md (Iterator row: disposed - traversal state is behavioral, not a doc invariant); fixtures/katas/iterator/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.4
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: with the sample covering all six emissions the conventional walk names e4_epsilon, so the unique set is empty (killed); the non-empty unique sets of the other entries are coverage, not modelling

expected.detail: the duplicate-emission replay fault (s5 re-emits epsilon) with the pre-registered sample extended to every emitted position: the conventional walk fails at position 5 (no declared element there) and names e4_epsilon, exactly the element both probe witnesses name. unique is empty - the parity ceiling for the whole kata.

commands: python3 prototype/iterator_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: complete sample [0..5] names element:e4_epsilon
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/iterator/duplicate-emission.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 2 findings

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/iterator_baseline.py --assert: a frozen position-sample smoke walk (emitted[i] = declared[i], naming both sides on failure; no total-length, termination or tail assertion), executed before the probe arm.

baseline.artifact: prototype/iterator_baseline.py sha256:d3cb5d6e7ad2ff7190346d55b1854d851e31354d105c56c433174941942a2277 (scripted position-sample smoke walk; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: identity as a kernel primitive (id_Step, id_Element)
expressibility_gap.why: the equation paths must be non-empty, so identity is encoded as the declared self-tables loop_step/loop_elem; the kernel cannot verify a self-table is the identity, so the round-trip equations are checked only relative to that declared data

expressibility_gap.invariant: the unique band is modelling advantage, not sampling coverage
expressibility_gap.why: a conventional complete sequence comparison catches every seeded multiplicity fault (duplicate-covered records the parity ceiling); the non-empty unique sets exist only where the pre-registered position sample does not look, so every survived verdict here is coverage-scoped

discrepancies: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md records the Iterator row as disposed (no executable invariant). This kata finds a traversal law on the declared emission table, but only with two named encodings: identity as declared self-tables and coverage through a declared inverse; order additionally needs modeled successor cells. No detection-rate claim is made.
procedure: 1. The law was named and the fault set, samples and expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/iterator/ (README.md, faults.json) before any recorded run; nothing above the observed-results section is edited after the run.

2. The conventional arm (prototype/iterator_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: a scripted position-sample smoke walk asserting emitted[i] = declared[i] for the pre-registered indices and naming both sides on failure; positions outside the sample (and total length, termination, the tail) are never inspected.

3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`; findings are recorded verbatim. The fixtures declare the traversal law as four constraints - arrow totality, the declarative key Step[yields] (injectivity), and the two accepted round-trip equations yields;back = loop_step and back;yields = loop_elem (coverage through the declared inverse).

4. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements element:<Element row name>; a key collision names the shared emission, a dangling on `back` names that element row, an equation violation names the element of its domain row (Step-domain rows through yields). unique_detections = sorted(probe elements) minus baseline-identified elements.

5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived. A silent probe on an order fault is a killed entry with the missing predicate named, never a fabricated finding.
